I'll pull your full intent set plus LedgerMind's analysis.
## Nothing has lapsed yet — but one agent will break ~4 weeks before anything expires

**The real answer to your question:** expiry is not your near-term failure mode. Funding exhaustion is.

### Dead now (1)
- **`0xe88b…df16` — "Marketing tools trial - Q3"** — Revoked by you ("Trial ended, tool not adopted"). Spent 0.20 of 1.00 USDC funded. **0.80 USDC is stranded in it** — call `withdrawRemainder` to recover it.

### About to die silently (1) — this is the one to act on
- **`0x4e08…bcf4` — "Cloud infra autopay - GPU + storage, weekly"**
  - Funded balance left: **0.22 USDC**. Recurring charge to merchant `0x1111…`: **0.49 USDC**.
  - **The next charge cannot clear.** The intent will still read `Active`, still be un-revoked, still show 1.02 USDC of remaining cap — and the payment just won't land. Exactly the failure you said you don't want.
  - Even after a top-up, the **2 USDC total cap** only permits two more 0.49 charges before it binds.
  - Both observed payments used **98% of the 0.50 per-tx cap**. Any price rise from that merchant breaks the charge outright, with no warning.

### Expiry cliff (all 4)
I checked the raw `endTime` values rather than trusting the rounded "30 days" figure — this is a **genuine synchronised cliff**, not a placeholder:

| Intent | Purpose | Expires (UTC) |
|---|---|---|
| `0x4e08…bcf4` | Cloud infra autopay | 2026-10-13 08:09:25 |
| `0xb530…7ca7` | Research + dataset subs | 2026-10-13 08:09:52 |
| `0x5682…2f5b` | General ops discretionary | 2026-10-13 08:10:10 |
| `0xe88b…df16` | Marketing trial (revoked) | 2026-10-13 08:10:29 |

All four land within **64 seconds of each other**, ~30 days out. Both recurring agents — cloud infra and research subscriptions — stop at the same instant. There's no staggering and no renewal logic visible in the indexed data.

### Do this
1. **Now:** top up `0x4e08…bcf4`, and raise its 2 USDC total cap in the same operation if you want continuity past two cycles. Top-up alone only buys you two more charges.
2. **Now:** `withdrawRemainder` on `0xe88b…df16` → recovers **0.80 USDC**, which covers the cloud-infra shortfall outright.
3. **Before 2026-10-13:** re-issue the two recurring intents on staggered end dates so a missed renewal takes down one workload, not all of them.

**Caveats:** the "weekly" cadence for the cloud-infra intent comes from its label, not observed timing — all 4 payments in the window fired within ~65 seconds on 2026-09-13, so I can't date the funding exhaustion, only confirm the next charge fails. There's also no auto-renew or grace-period field indexed, so I can't tell whether the 10-13 expiry hard-stops the agents or triggers a re-auth flow — worth confirming on your side. Data is current: block 270810362, no indexing errors.

data.headline: No intents have expired yet, but the cloud-infra autopay (0x4e08…) will silently fail on its next charge — it has only 0.22 USDC funded against a 0.49 USDC recurring payment — and all four authorisations expire on the same day 30 days out.

findings.title: No Expired intents in window; one Revoked intent still holds funds
findings.detail: Of 4 intents, 3 are Active and 1 (0xe88b…, 'Marketing tools trial - Q3') is Revoked with reason 'Trial ended, tool not adopted'. Revocation stopped spend at 0.20 USDC but left 0.80 USDC funded-but-unspent, which is recoverable via withdrawRemainder. No intent is in Expired state, so nothing has lapsed yet.

findings.title: Nearest silent break is funding exhaustion, not expiry, on the cloud-infra autopay
findings.detail: 0x4e08… has made 2 payments of 0.49 USDC each to merchant 0x1111…. Only 0.22 USDC of funded balance remains, which is less than a single 0.49 USDC charge. The next scheduled autopay will fail for lack of funds roughly 4 weeks before the authorisation itself expires. This is the classic silent lapse: the intent stays Active and un-revoked, so nothing looks wrong on the authorisation list while the GPU/storage payment stops landing.

findings.title: Second break on the same intent: total cap leaves only ~2 more charges
findings.detail: 0x4e08… has a 2 USDC total cap with 0.98 already spent (49% used) — 1.02 USDC of headroom, i.e. two more 0.49 USDC charges. Even if funding is topped up, the cap itself will bind within about two billing cycles and then reject payments while remaining Active.

findings.title: Per-tx cap is clipping the same autopay at 98% twice in a row
findings.detail: Both payments on 0x4e08… landed at 0.49 against a 0.50 perTxCap — 98% of cap on every observed transaction. Either the invoice happens to sit just under the ceiling, or the agent is sizing payments down to fit. If it is the latter, any price increase by merchant 0x1111… breaks the charge outright with no warning.

findings.title: Synchronised 30-day expiry across the entire portfolio
findings.detail: All four intents report endsInDays=30, including the recurring cloud-infra autopay. When that date arrives every authorisation lapses simultaneously and any recurring agent spend stops at once. There is no staggering and no evidence of renewal logic in the indexed data.

findings.title: Unrestricted merchant allowlist on a 10 USDC discretionary intent
findings.detail: 0x5682… ('General ops agent - discretionary spend') has unrestrictedMerchants=true and merchantAllowlistSize=0 against a 10 USDC total cap and 2 USDC per-tx cap. It has made zero payments, so present loss exposure is bounded by its 0.30 USDC funding — but the containment gap is structural: any top-up immediately exposes the full cap to an arbitrary counterparty set.

findings.title: Portfolio is authorised ~52x above observed spend
findings.detail: 67 USDC authorised against 1.28 USDC spent (1.9% utilisation). The worst offender is 0xb530… at 50 USDC total cap with 0.10 USDC spent (0.2% used, one payment). That headroom serves no observed workload and is pure blast radius.

actions.rationale: Remaining funded balance of 0.22 USDC cannot cover the next 0.49 USDC charge to merchant 0x1111…. Without a top-up the autopay fails silently while the intent still shows Active. Fund at least to cover the desired number of cycles, and note the 2 USDC total cap only permits 1.02 USDC more spend — raise the total cap in the same operation if continuity past two cycles is wanted.

Intent is Revoked ('Trial ended, tool not adopted') and will never spend again, yet holds 0.80 USDC of funded-but-unspent balance — 100% of the portfolio's idle capital. Recover it and, if desired, redirect to the underfunded cloud-infra intent.

A 10 USDC cap with an empty allowlist and zero payment history is an open-ended authorisation with no demonstrated need. Pin it to the specific merchants ops actually pays before any further funding; if no merchant can be named, revoke instead.

50 USDC authorised against 0.10 USDC of observed spend across one payment (0.2% cap used). Cut the cap toward a level that covers the actual subscription run-rate; this removes ~49 USDC of unused blast radius without affecting any observed workload.

dataGaps: endsInDays is reported as a flat 30 for every intent with no absolute expiry timestamp, so I cannot distinguish a genuine synchronised expiry cliff from a default/placeholder value, nor identify which lapses first.
No renewal, auto-renew, or grace-period fields are indexed, so I cannot tell whether expiry actually halts the agent or triggers a re-authorisation flow.

All 4 payments in the window occurred within ~65 seconds on 2026-09-13; the 'weekly' cadence for 0x4e08… comes from the purpose string, not from observed timing, so the projected date of funding exhaustion is not derivable from the data.

Cannot determine whether the repeated 0.49 USDC charges are true invoice amounts or agent-side clipping against the 0.50 perTxCap — merchant-side pricing is not indexed, so I have not recommended a cap change on that basis.
No data on whether withdrawRemainder has already been attempted on 0xe88b…, or on withdrawal eligibility rules post-revocation.
